_comment: Madeira dependency catalogue. Each entry says what a Windows component is, how it can be satisfied on Madeira's iOS/Wine stack, and the exact Wine-side action that satisfies it. 'support' is about Madeira, not about upstream Wine: builtin = Wine/DXMT already provides it; override = only DLL overrides / registry / environment / Windows version are needed; payload = needs native DLL files (bundled or dropped in Documents/madeira-compat/dlls); manual = needs running a separate Windows installer, not attempted yet; partial = some titles work; unsupported = cannot work on iOS. Sources: Winetricks verbs, Bottles dependencies, Protonfixes game scripts.

vcrun6.title: Visual C++ 6 runtime
vcrun6.summary: Visual C++ 6 SP4 libraries (msvcrt, mfc42, msvcp60).
vcrun6.notes: Wine ships msvcrt and a partial mfc42; games that ship their own mfc42 in the install folder load it first anyway.

vcrun2005.title: Visual C++ 2005 runtime
vcrun2005.notes: Wine has no msvcr80/msvcp80 builtin; native DLLs are needed.

vcrun2010.title: Visual C++ 2010 runtime
vcrun2010.summary: Visual C++ 2010 libraries (atl100, mfc100, msvcp100, msvcr100, vcomp100).

vcrun2012.title: Visual C++ 2012 runtime
vcrun2012.summary: Visual C++ 2012 libraries (atl110, mfc110, msvcp110, msvcr110, vcomp110).

vcrun2013.title: Visual C++ 2013 runtime
vcrun2013.summary: Visual C++ 2013 libraries (atl120, mfc120, msvcp120, msvcr120, vcomp120).

vcrun2015.title: Visual C++ 2015 runtime
vcrun2015.summary: Visual C++ 2015 (14.0) libraries: msvcp140, vcruntime140, vccorlib140, concrt140.
vcrun2015.notes: Madeira ships the x86_64 Microsoft VC++ 2015-2022 runtime DLLs in the app bundle (x86_64-vcruntime/), so 64-bit games are covered without any download.

vcrun2019.title: Visual C++ 2015-2019 runtime
vcrun2019.notes: 64-bit is bundled; a 32-bit (WoW64) title needs the i386 DLLs under Documents/madeira-compat/dlls/i386/.

vcrun2022.title: Visual C++ 2015-2022 runtime
vcrun2022.summary: Visual C++ 2015-2022 (14.3) libraries, superset of vcrun2019.

ucrtbase2019.title: Universal C Runtime (2019)
ucrtbase2019.summary: api-ms-win-crt-* / ucrtbase, provided by Wine's builtin ucrtbase.

mfc42.title: Microsoft Foundation Classes 4.2
mfc42.summary: mfc42.dll / mfc42u.dll used by pre-2005 Visual C++ programs.

mfc40.title: Microsoft Foundation Classes 4.0
mfc40.summary: mfc40.dll used by very old Visual C++ 4.x programs.

d3dx9.title: DirectX 9 d3dx9 helper libraries
d3dx9.summary: d3dx9_24..d3dx9_43 (D3DX math, shader and texture helpers). Wine implements none of these natively.
d3dx9.notes: Most D3D9 titles only need d3dx9_43; a game that also imports an older d3dx9_NN will need that DLL too.

d3dx9_43.title: DirectX 9 d3dx9_43.dll
d3dx9_43.summary: The single d3dx9 DLL most D3D9 games import.

d3dx11_43.title: DirectX 11 d3dx11_43.dll
d3dx11_43.summary: D3DX11 helpers for D3D11 games (D3DX11CompileFromFile and friends).

d3dcompiler_43.title: DirectX d3dcompiler_43.dll
d3dcompiler_43.summary: D3D shader compiler 43. Wine ships a complete builtin implementation.

d3dcompiler_47.title: DirectX d3dcompiler_47.dll
d3dcompiler_47.summary: D3D shader compiler 47. Wine ships a complete builtin implementation, which is what DXMT's d3d11 uses.

directx9.title: DirectX 9 runtime (June 2010)
directx9.summary: The DirectX 9.0c redistributable installs d3dx9/d3dx11/xact/xinput/dsound/directplay at once. Winetricks treats the all-in-one verb as deprecated.
directx9.notes: Prefer the individual dependencies (d3dx9, d3dcompiler_*, xact, xinput, directplay, directmusic).

xinput.title: Microsoft XInput (Xbox controller)
xinput.summary: xinput1_1..1_4 / xinput9_1_0. Madeira's Winios implements XInput over the host gamepad, so the builtin is used.
xinput.notes: Gamepad support itself is a Madeira runtime feature (WiniosGamepad); the override just keeps games on the builtin.

dinput8.title: DirectInput 8
dinput8.summary: Wine's builtin dinput8 talks to Madeira's DirectInput bridge.
dinput8.notes: Some games ship a native dinput8 proxy (e.g. DSfix); if one sits next to the exe it is loaded first regardless, so this override is builtin by default.

directplay.title: Microsoft DirectPlay
directplay.summary: dplayx.dll and friends, from the DirectX 9 user redistributable.
directplay.notes: Only needed by games using the obsolete DirectPlay networking API.

directmusic.title: Microsoft DirectMusic
directmusic.notes: Provides the legacy MIDI/DLS synthesis path for older games.

xact.title: Microsoft XACT Engine
xact.summary: xactengine2_0..3_7 plus X3DAudio and XAPOFX: the DirectX audio engine many D3D9/D3D10 era games use for sound effects.

xaudio29.title: XAudio 2.9
xaudio29.summary: xaudio2_9.dll used by DirectX 11/12 era games; Wine has xaudio2_7 but not 2_8/2_9.

openal.title: OpenAL 1.1
openal.summary: OpenAL32.dll / wrap_oal.dll, used by id Tech and many 2000s games.
openal.notes: Native OpenAL is only needed by games that load it directly; games using FAudio/XAudio are unaffected.

dsound.title: DirectSound
dsound.summary: Wine's builtin dsound on FAudio, routed to Madeira's AudioToolbox backend.

physx.title: NVIDIA PhysX (legacy runtime)
physx.summary: PhysXLoader.dll / PhysXCore.dll / NxCharacter.dll, the pre-2.8 PhysX runtime many 2005-2010 games link.
physx.notes: Games that bundle newer PhysX DLLs next to the exe load those first; this only covers titles that expect it in system32. GPU PhysX is not available through Metal.

dotnet20.title: .NET Framework 2.0
dotnet20.summary: Microsoft .NET Framework 2.0. Madeira ships wine-mono, which runs many .NET 2.0-era managed games without the Microsoft runtime.
dotnet20.notes: Installing the Microsoft .NET installer is not attempted automatically on iOS; wine-mono is the default and usually enough for XNA/Unity-ish managed titles.

dotnet35.title: .NET Framework 3.5
dotnet35.summary: .NET 3.5 including WPF and LINQ, on top of 2.0. wine-mono covers much of it.

dotnet40.title: .NET Framework 4.0
dotnet40.summary: .NET 4.0. wine-mono implements a large part of the 4.x BCL.
dotnet40.notes: Managed games that work under wine-mono need no action; ones that do not are reported as needing the Microsoft runtime, which is not installed automatically.

dotnet48.title: .NET Framework 4.8
dotnet48.summary: .NET 4.8, the last 4.x Framework. wine-mono handles a good share of 4.x titles.

quartz.title: DirectShow quartz.dll
quartz.summary: Native quartz.dll DirectShow filter graph manager. Wine's builtin quartz has no working video decoders on iOS.
quartz.notes: Madeira's winegstreamer supplies the WMA/MP3/WAV/MP4 decode path; a game that only needs those plays without native quartz.

qedit.title: DirectShow Editing Services (qedit.dll)
qedit.summary: DirectShow sample grabber and editing services.

devenum.title: DirectShow device enumerator (devenum.dll)
devenum.summary: Enumerates DirectShow filters for games that build their own graph.

amstream.title: DirectShow multimedia stream (amstream.dll)
amstream.summary: Media stream filter used by some video-playback code paths.

icodecs.title: Indeo codecs
icodecs.summary: Indeo 4/5 video decoder, used by FMV in 1990s titles.

l3codecx.title: MPEG Layer-3 DirectShow decoder
l3codecx.summary: Wine's builtin l3codecx.ax, the DirectShow filter a title asks for by name. It decodes MPEG Layer-3 audio without Microsoft's legacy DirectX redistributable.
l3codecx.notes: Winetricks installs Microsoft's native l3codecx.ax out of the DirectX redistributable; Wine builds the same filter, so the builtin one is pinned rather than an installer the prefix would have to accept.

mediafoundation.title: Media Foundation
mediafoundation.summary: mfplat/mf/mfreadwrite. Madeira's winegstreamer supplies the unix media source; DXMT/Wine provide the PE side.
mediafoundation.notes: 64-bit processes only get the real Media Foundation unix side with MADEIRA_WG_64BIT=1; 32-bit (WoW64) processes get it by default (compat/rules.json sets it for 64-bit images that import these). mfcore is the Windows 10 split of the same pipeline; Wine has no separate mfcore module, so a title that imports it by name resolves against Wine's mf.

mf.title: Media Foundation video playback
mf.summary: Alias for mediafoundation used by some game fixes; selects the winegstreamer Media Foundation source.
mf.notes: For a game whose intro video shows a black screen, MADEIRA_WG_64BIT=1 plus the mfplat/mf/mfreadwrite overrides is the usual fix.

wmp9.title: Windows Media Player 9
wmp9.summary: WMP9 runtime used by games that embed the WMP ActiveX control.

corefonts.title: Microsoft core fonts
corefonts.summary: Arial, Courier New, Times New Roman, Comic Sans, Andale, Impact, Trebuchet, Verdana, Webdings.
corefonts.notes: Drop the .ttf files in Documents/madeira-compat/fonts/ to install them.

arial.title: Arial font
arial.summary: Arial required by a game's UI.

verdana.title: Verdana font
verdana.summary: Verdana required by a game's UI.

tahoma.title: Tahoma font
tahoma.summary: Tahoma required by a game's UI.

courier.title: Courier New font
courier.summary: Courier New required by a game's console or UI.

trebuchet.title: Trebuchet MS font
trebuchet.summary: Trebuchet MS required by a game's UI.

lucida.title: Lucida fonts
lucida.summary: Lucida Console / Lucida Sans, used by a few console fontsets.

segoe_script.title: Segoe Script font
segoe_script.summary: Segoe Script, required by some modern UI.

msxml4.title: MSXML 4.0
msxml4.summary: msxml4.dll (MSXML2.DOMDocument.4.0 and the Msxml2 4.0 side-by-side assembly). Wine's builtin, which shares msxml3's parser, is in both farms; the native-msxml recipe can still put a native copy first.

msxml3.title: MSXML 3.0
msxml3.summary: msxml3.dll XML parser used by older installers and games.

msxml6.title: MSXML 6.0
msxml6.summary: msxml6.dll XML parser used by modern launchers and games.

gdiplus.title: GDI+
gdiplus.summary: Wine's builtin gdiplus is complete enough for games and launchers.

riched20.title: RichEdit 2.0
riched20.summary: riched20.dll used for in-game text input and help.

msftedit.title: RichEdit 4.1 (msftedit.dll)
msftedit.summary: msftedit.dll used by newer text controls.

wsh57.title: Windows Script Host 5.7
wsh57.summary: jscript/scrrun/vbscript/cscript used by some launchers and installers.

jet40.title: Microsoft Jet 4.0 (Access database)
jet40.summary: Jet 4.0 database engine, needed by games with Access-based data.

xna31.title: XNA Framework 3.1
xna31.summary: XNA 3.1 managed framework for XNA games.
xna31.notes: XNA is a managed framework; wine-mono plus the XNA redistributable is the usual path.

xna40.title: XNA Framework 4.0
xna40.summary: XNA 4.0 managed framework for XNA games.

gfw.title: Games for Windows LIVE
gfw.summary: Games for Windows LIVE (GFWL) client, required by a handful of GFWL-era titles.
gfw.notes: GFWL needs a live Microsoft online service that no longer exists for most titles.

cnc-ddraw.title: cnc-ddraw
cnc-ddraw.summary: Madeira ships cnc-ddraw (third_party/cnc-ddraw, MIT) for 32-bit DirectDraw games, presenting through DXMT's Direct3D 9. Opt-in per game: the cnc-ddraw recipe, or env.MADEIRA_DDRAW = cnc.

dgvoodoo2.title: dgVoodoo2
dgvoodoo2.summary: DirectDraw/Direct3D 8/9 to Direct3D 11 wrapper. Converts to D3D11, which DXMT then maps to Metal, but dgVoodoo2 needs a full D3D11 feature set that is not available here.
dgvoodoo2.notes: Not useful on Madeira; the DXMT path already covers D3D11 games.

eac.title: Easy Anti-Cheat
eac.notes: Anti-cheat needs a kernel driver and deep process integrity that iOS does not permit. Online anti-cheat titles cannot be supported; single-player games that merely bundle EAC often run without it.

battleye.title: BattlEye
battleye.notes: Same constraint as Easy Anti-Cheat; single-player/offline content is unaffected.

anticheat-generic.title: Kernel anti-cheat (other)
anticheat-generic.summary: The other anti-cheat runtimes a Windows build can carry: Riot Vanguard, EQU8, XIGNCODE3, nProtect GameGuard, HackShield, Arxan and similar.
anticheat-generic.notes: Every one of these installs a kernel driver or a protected service and checks the process from outside; iOS does not permit that, so an online protected title cannot run. An offline title that merely links the client library often starts anyway, which is why this is reported as a compatibility case rather than refused at launch.

denuvo.title: Denuvo DRM
denuvo.notes: DRM layers that rely on tight Windows/hypervisor integration cannot be supported. Prefer DRM-free (GOG) builds of the same game.

drm-generic.title: Copy protection (other)
drm-generic.summary: The other copy-protection runtimes: VMProtect, Themida, SafeDisc, SecuROM, StarForce and the disc checks they perform.
drm-generic.notes: These read the original disc, virtualise the code or check the kernel; none of that is possible on iOS. A DRM-free build of the same title is the way to play it.

winhttp.title: Windows HTTP Services
winhttp.summary: Wine's builtin winhttp/wininet, used for online checks and launchers.

devenum-winrt.title: Windows Runtime activation (WinRT)
devenum-winrt.summary: Windows Runtime activation factories used by a few UWP-derived engines (e.g. Unity's WinRT video path).
devenum-winrt.notes: Madeira's wine build handles the common activation-factory fallbacks; RoInitialize is available.

mfplat.title: Media Foundation platform
mfplat.summary: mfplat/mfreadwrite/mf: the Media Foundation pipeline some 2013+ titles use for video and audio decoding.

wmv9vcm.title: Windows Media Video 9 codec
wmv9vcm.summary: wmvdecod/wmasf: WMV and VC-1 playback for intros and cutscenes.

d3d8.title: Direct3D 8
d3d8.summary: Madeira's d3d8.dll (32-bit) is third_party/d3d8to9: Direct3D 8 translated to DXMT's Direct3D 9 (Metal); Wine's own d3d8 needs wined3d, which has no backend here. A d3d8.dll the game ships beside itself still wins (n,b). There is no 64-bit d3d8 (Windows never had one).

ddraw.title: DirectDraw
ddraw.summary: The DirectDraw path cnc-ddraw and native ddraw replace for 1998-2003 titles.

d3d9.title: Direct3D 9
d3d9.summary: The D3D9 runtime, served by Wine's d3d9 and DXMT.

d3dx10.title: DirectX 10 D3DX helpers
d3dx10.summary: d3dx10_43/d3dx10_42 helper libraries, which Wine does not implement.

richeld30.title: Rich Edit 3.0
richeld30.summary: riched30.dll, needed by a few older tools and launchers.

msi.title: Windows Installer
msi.summary: Wine's builtin msi runs MSI packages, including the MSI payload inside a self-extracting redistributable. Both farms ship msi.dll and msiexec.exe: the 64-bit one gained them (installer_scripting in build/wine-pe/arm64ec-farm.json) so x64 packages and custom actions run too.

mfc140.title: MFC 14 (Visual C++ 2015+)
mfc140.summary: mfc140/mfc140u, the MFC part of the modern VC++ redistributable.

msvcr71.title: Visual C++ 7.1 runtime
msvcr71.summary: msvcr71/msvcp71/mfc71, the Visual Studio .NET 2003 runtime used by 2003-2006 titles.

vb6run.title: Visual Basic 6 runtime
vb6run.summary: msvbvm60.dll, required by Visual Basic 6 programs and a surprising number of 2000s games and launchers.

vjrun20.title: Visual J# 2.0 runtime
vjrun20.summary: Required by the handful of .NET-era Java titles.

dotnet35sp1.title: .NET Framework 3.5 SP1
dotnet35sp1.summary: A few late-2000s titles and launchers need 3.5 SP1 specifically.

dotnetcore3.title: .NET Core 3.x
dotnetcore3.summary: Self-contained .NET Core deployments usually work without this; a framework-dependent one needs it.

powershell.title: Windows PowerShell
powershell.summary: A few installers and launchers run PowerShell scripts.

wininet.title: Windows Internet (wininet)
wininet.summary: HTTP/FTP API used by launchers and updaters.

urlmon.title: URL moniker (urlmon)
urlmon.summary: Downloads and monikers for embedded browser controls.

webview2.title: Microsoft Edge WebView2
webview2.summary: Store clients and launchers that render their UI in WebView2.

allfonts.title: All bundled fonts
allfonts.summary: The full font set winetricks installs, for engines that measure text against specific faces.

sourcehansans.title: Source Han Sans (CJK)
sourcehansans.summary: CJK-capable sans font for Japanese, Korean and Chinese titles.

fakechinese.title: Chinese locale fonts
fakechinese.summary: Chinese glyph coverage for titles that ship none.

ubisoftconnect.title: Ubisoft Connect
ubisoftconnect.summary: Ubisoft's client and its DRM cannot run on Madeira.

xact_x64.title: XACT Engine (64-bit)
xact_x64.summary: 64-bit xactengine3_7, for titles whose 64-bit build links it.

usp10.title: Uniscribe (usp10)
usp10.summary: Script shaping for complex text; Wine's builtin usually suffices.

d3dxof.title: DirectX 3DXOF
d3dxof.summary: d3dxof.dll parses .x files, used by some 2000s engines.

wine-version.title: Windows version override
wine-version.summary: Windows version reported to the game, set per executable so titles cannot affect each other.

esync.title: esync
esync.summary: A Linux wineserver feature; Madeira has no Linux kernel to use it.

fsync.title: fsync
fsync.summary: A Linux wineserver feature; Madeira has no Linux kernel to use it.

nvapi.title: NVIDIA NVAPI
nvapi.summary: NVIDIA-only API; Madeira runs on Apple silicon.

gamescope.title: Gamescope compositor
gamescope.summary: A Linux Wayland compositor; Madeira presents through Metal.

dxvk.title: DXVK / VKD3D
dxvk.summary: Vulkan-based D3D translation. Madeira uses DXMT and Metal instead, so a DXVK-only launch option has no equivalent.

d3dcompiler-legacy.title: DirectX shader compiler, older versions
d3dcompiler-legacy.summary: The d3dcompiler_33 to _42 and _46 DLLs. Wine ships one complete builtin implementation for each of those version numbers (both farms), so a game that links an older compiler still compiles its shaders. d3dcompiler_44 and _45 were Windows 8 preview builds that Wine does not build: a program importing one is reported as an unavailable module, not answered here.

xaudio2-legacy.title: XAudio2 2.0 to 2.7
xaudio2-legacy.summary: XAudio2 before 2.8, which many 2007-2013 games link. Wine's builtin xaudio2 serves every version number, so no native redistributable is needed.

miles-sound.title: Miles Sound System (mss32)
miles-sound.summary: mss32.dll ships with the game and is a self-contained Windows mixer, so it usually runs through FEX as it is. It is listed so a title whose audio fails is classified as audio and not as something else.
miles-sound.notes: When a Miles title is silent, the fix is usually the Sound Blaster/EAX setting inside the game's own options.

bink2.title: Bink 2 video
bink2.summary: bink2w32/bink2w64 ship with the game and decode video through the CPU, so playback normally works. A title whose intro video is black or skipped is a video compatibility case.

smacker.title: Smacker video
smacker.summary: smackw32.dll, the RAD video format used by 1990s titles, shipped with the game. Decoding is pure software.

fmod.title: FMOD audio
fmod.summary: fmod.dll / fmodex.dll ship with the game and mix audio themselves, so they normally run as they are; 3D audio can differ because there is no Creative EAX device.

epic-online-services.title: Epic Online Services
epic-online-services.summary: EOSSDK ships with an Epic or Epic-published game. Offline and single-player play works; anything that needs the Epic account service does not.

gog-galaxy.title: GOG Galaxy
gog-galaxy.summary: Galaxy.dll is the GOG client integration. A DRM-free GOG install runs without it; achievements and playtime need the client.

steamworks.title: Steamworks API
steamworks.summary: steam_api.dll comes from Steam itself; Madeira Dock starts Steam so the API has a client to talk to. A Steam game installed DRM-free also runs with the client closed where the game allows it.

vendor-gpu-libraries.title: GPU vendor libraries
vendor-gpu-libraries.summary: NVAPI, NVNGX, AMD AGS/AMF and the third-party SDKs (Aftermath, SSAO, WaveWorks). There is no NVIDIA or AMD driver behind Metal, so the Wine stubs answer them: a game that merely queries them keeps running, and one that refuses to start without the real library is reported instead of crashing.
vendor-gpu-libraries.notes: The Protonfixes 'disable NVAPI' fix has the same intent on Linux; on Madeira the Wine stub is the only implementation there can be.

intel-oodle.title: Oodle data compression
intel-oodle.summary: oo2core ships with Unreal Engine titles and is a plain Windows DLL, so it decompresses through FEX. It is listed because its slow path is a common cause of long loads rather than a failure.

ucrt-api-sets.title: Universal CRT API sets
ucrt-api-sets.summary: The api-ms-win-crt-* forwarder DLLs that any program built with the Windows 10 SDK imports. Wine's ucrtbase provides every one of them.

d3d10-d3d11.title: Direct3D 10 and 11
d3d10-d3d11.summary: Madeira translates Direct3D 10 and 11 to Metal through DXMT, which is the d3d11 and dxgi implementation in its Wine tree. A game importing them needs nothing installed.
d3d10-d3d11.notes: There is one file per family here, as in Wine: dxgi.dll, d3d11.dll and d3d10*.dll. A title that links one of the versioned names (d3d11_1.dll, dxgi1_2.dll and up) is asking for a file no Wine build ships, and the interfaces it wants are in dxgi.dll and d3d11.dll already.

d3d12-madeira.title: Direct3D 12
d3d12-madeira.summary: Direct3D 12 through Madeira's own d3d12.dll (build/madeira-d3d12, Metal), not Wine's vkd3d-based one, which needs Vulkan. It is a newer path than D3D11, so a title that offers both may be steadier on D3D11.
d3d12-madeira.notes: Only d3d12 is claimed. dxil.dll and dxcompiler.dll are the DirectX Shader Compiler redistributables rather than system files: a title that links them ships them beside itself, and the engine reports such an import as one the program brings. D3D12Core.dll is the Agility SDK runtime a game ships in its own folder for d3d12.dll to load; Wine's d3d12core needs Vulkan and is not in either farm, so it is not claimed here either.

vulkan.title: Vulkan
vulkan.summary: Madeira presents through Metal and has no Vulkan driver, so a game that insists on a Vulkan device cannot start. Most titles that import vulkan-1.dll also offer Direct3D; forcing the Direct3D renderer in the game's own settings or launch arguments is the fix.

openvr.title: OpenVR / SteamVR
openvr.summary: There is no SteamVR runtime on iOS and no headset to drive, so a VR-only title cannot run.

chromium-embedded.title: Chromium Embedded Framework
chromium-embedded.summary: libcef.dll drives the launcher or in-game browser of some titles. It is a large Windows build that runs through FEX; when it is the launcher itself, the game can often be started directly from its own executable instead.

wxwidgets.title: wxWidgets
wxwidgets.summary: wxmsw*.dll belongs to a launcher or configuration tool shipped with the game rather than to the game itself.

physx-3.title: NVIDIA PhysX 3
physx-3.summary: The 2.8-era and 3.x PhysX runtimes (PhysXCooking, PhysX3Common, APEX) that ship inside the game folder. They are Windows DLLs and run through FEX, which is also why they are slow; the game's own physics setting is the lever.

qt.title: Qt
qt.summary: Qt5/Qt6 DLLs belong to a launcher or tool shipped with the game; the game itself usually lives beside it.

dxva2.title: Hardware video decoding (DXVA2)
dxva2.summary: There is no DXVA2 video device behind Metal. A title that plays video through it falls back to software decoding or to another path; playback may stutter.

vcrun-uwp.title: Visual C++ runtime, store apps
vcrun-uwp.summary: The *_app variants of the Visual C++ 2015-2022 runtime, used by Microsoft Store and Game Pass builds. The desktop runtime does not satisfy them.

wine-mono.title: Wine Mono (.NET runtime)
wine-mono.summary: Wine's own .NET implementation, the MSI Wine installs into a prefix so managed programs run without Microsoft's .NET installers. Titles built with .NET need it, and Wine stops a program the first time one starts to ask for it.
wine-mono.notes: Wine installs the MSI from share/wine/mono of the runtime at prefix creation; the engine can only report that it is needed. Winlator ships these two files with its prefixes (winlator:wine_addons) and blocks Microsoft's .NET installers, which Madeira's Wine does not need.

wine-gecko.title: Wine Gecko (HTML engine)
wine-gecko.summary: Wine's HTML engine, the MSI Wine installs into a prefix for programs that embed a browser control or show an HTML page. Without it the first such program stops to ask for it, or shows an empty page.
wine-gecko.notes: Installed by Wine from share/wine/gecko of the runtime at prefix creation. Launchers that embed a browser control want it; a browser-based launcher that fails without it can also be skipped with the launcher-webview recipe.

d3dcsx.title: Direct3D CSX (compute shader extensions)
d3dcsx.summary: The d3dcsx helpers (scan, sort, prefix sum) that Direct3D 10 and 11 titles link against for GPU sorting and particle work. Winlator installs them with its Direct3D component.

opengl.title: OpenGL
opengl.summary: Wine's opengl32.dll drives a host OpenGL context. Madeira presents through DXMT and Metal and has no GL driver, so a title whose only renderer is OpenGL cannot start; most titles that import opengl32.dll also offer Direct3D, and choosing it in the game's own settings or launch arguments is the fix.
opengl.notes: The module is in the Wine tree, so it is not a missing file; it is a path with no backend here. Engines that probe GL first (id Tech 3/4, older SDL builds, some launchers) can be pointed at Direct3D without a Wine change.

epic-online-services.title: Epic Online Services
epic-online-services.summary: EOSSDK-Win64-Shipping.dll, the Epic Online Services SDK a game ships beside its own executable for sign-in, achievements, friends and matchmaking.
epic-online-services.notes: The SDK is inside the game folder and runs through FEX. A single-player title starts without the Epic client; sign-in, achievements and multiplayer need it, which Madeira does not run.

ubisoft-connect.title: Ubisoft Connect
ubisoft-connect.summary: uplay_r1_loader / uplay_r2_loader / upc_r2_loader, the Ubisoft client integration layer a Ubisoft title loads at startup.
ubisoft-connect.notes: The loader is game-side and runs under Wine. Titles where it only carries achievements start without the client; titles that use it as their DRM need Ubisoft Connect running, which Madeira does not install.

ea-app.title: EA app / Origin
ea-app.summary: The Origin/EA app integration a modern EA title loads at startup (origin, eaapp, igoproxy64).
ea-app.notes: Same split as the other store clients: the integration library runs, the client it talks to is not installed, so a title that needs a signed-in client does not start.

discord-sdk.title: Discord Game SDK
discord-sdk.summary: discord_game_sdk.dll, shipped by many titles for Discord Rich Presence and voice.
discord-sdk.notes: Nothing to configure: the shipped DLL initialises without the Discord client and the game runs. Presence and voice simply do not appear.

gfwl.title: Games for Windows LIVE
gfwl.summary: xlive.dll, the Games for Windows LIVE client and sign-in layer a 2007-2013 era title loads at startup.
gfwl.notes: Neither Wine nor Madeira ships xlive.dll, the client is not installable here, and the LIVE service was shut down in 2014, so a title that needs sign-in, achievements or multiplayer stops at its login dialog. Titles that only link xlive.dll and run offline are marked runnable in the library; nothing installable changes that.

dstorage.title: DirectStorage
dstorage.summary: DirectStorage (dstorage.dll / dstoragecore.dll) streams game assets through the GPU and an NVMe queue instead of through file reads.
dstorage.notes: Wine has no DirectStorage implementation (it is not one of its modules) and there is no NVMe queue to hand it, so a title that requires it for asset streaming cannot load its data. Most titles that import it keep a plain file path behind a launch option or a configuration setting.
